owned_invariants: The task names one of three schemas: coboundary_potential (edges, c), l1_dual_circulation (edges, w, and cap, which is 1 on every edge when absent) or canonical_rational (A and b as in WF7). A task the host cannot read, or that names another schema, is refused before anything is asked.
One question is asked, the task as written. The reply is an object with schema and certificate, the certificate an object.
no_float is recorded first. It fails for any number with a fraction or an exponent, and any text written like one, anywhere in the certificate, and the run is refused as FLOAT_IN_CERTIFICATE.

well_typed is recorded next. It fails unless the reply names the task's schema and the certificate has exactly the schema's fields, each of the right shape, with entries that are integers or text p/q. The run is then refused as ILL_TYPED.

Only then are the equations evaluated, each as its own predicate: coboundary_potential checks that c is the coboundary of phi on every edge; l1_dual_circulation checks that r is w plus the coboundary of f, that z is a circulation, that z is within the caps, and that the duality gap is zero; canonical_rational checks that the system has one solution, that x is it, and that every text entry is written as an integer or as p/q in lowest terms with q above 1.
The run is certified as CERTIFICATE_VALID with the schema when every predicate passed.
